# =====================================================================
# Sefer languages (2026-11-10, docs/spec/2026-11-10-sefer-languages.md).
# Tunables for how much a book's language matters. The per-work values
# (kehillah_lib_fluency_<work>, kehillah_lib_mastery_chance_<work>) are
# generated by scripts/kehillah_library_catalog.py in
# kehillah_library_language_values.txt.
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The chance a reading ends in mastery (kehillah_lib_mastery_chance_<work>,
# generated). Daniel, 2026-11-10: Learning should make a book much harder or
# easier, but any book can be tried; the picker shows every term. Before
# this, mastery was a fixed check: Learning 10 (8 under Talmud Torah).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
kehillah_study_chance_base = 50
# Learning: 4 points of chance for each point above or below 10, so Learning
# 10 is an even chance, 20 is near certain and 0 near hopeless.
kehillah_study_chance_learning_term = {
	value = learning
	subtract = 10
	multiply = 4
}
kehillah_study_chance_min = 5
kehillah_study_chance_max = 95
# Talmud Torah (was a Learning 8 floor instead of 10: two points of Learning).
kehillah_study_chance_talmud_torah = 8
# A book in a language the reader does not know (vanilla's knows_language):
# Saadia's Judeo-Arabic for an Ashkenazi rabbi, or Hebrew for a Jew without
# schooling. Revision 6 (Daniel, 2026-11-10): harsher, was -30.
kehillah_study_chance_foreign = -50
# Instead of that, when the language is a liturgical tongue of his faith
# (kehillah_liturgical_language_trigger): he knows its letters and many of
# its words from prayer. One term (revision 5), shrinking by
# kehillah_study_chance_liturgical_step for each book he masters in it,
# until at kehillah_language_readings_to_learn masteries he knows the
# language and has no penalty at all: -30, -20, -10, learned (revision 6;
# was -15 in steps of 5).
kehillah_study_chance_liturgical = -30
kehillah_study_chance_liturgical_step = 10
# Revision 6 (Daniel: "let it be counteracted by studying at a yeshiva or
# having your Dayyan study with you if they know the liturgical language").
# Each offsets the liturgical penalty only, never past zero
# (kehillah_study_chance_yeshiva_<language>, _dayyan_<language>, generated):
#  - a yeshiva: he is its student, or his community has one
#    (kehillah_language_yeshiva_help_trigger);
#  - the Dayyan of his community knows the language
#    (kehillah_language_dayyan_help_trigger).
kehillah_study_chance_yeshiva_help = 15
kehillah_study_chance_dayyan_help = 15
# Depth in the book's field (the Rabbi trait's track at 50 / 100; a
# Karaite's Scholar experience at 50).
kehillah_study_chance_depth_some = 5
kehillah_study_chance_depth_deep = 10
# The reader's personal tenet is one the book argues for (or against).
kehillah_study_chance_tenet_fit = 10
# Diligent, Lazy (negative), Scholar; Theologian.
kehillah_study_chance_trait = 10
kehillah_study_chance_trait_minor = 5
# A book he has mastered before.
kehillah_study_chance_reread = 20

# Books in a liturgical tongue of the reader's faith he must master before
# he has learned it (revision 5: only a mastered reading counts; it was any
# completed reading, and 2). Other languages are not learned by reading
# (Daniel: Arabic should be very difficult, for a Jew).
kehillah_language_readings_to_learn = 3

# The liturgical term and its two offsets for each language a sefer can be
# written in are generated (kehillah_study_chance_liturgical_<language> and
# friends, in kehillah_library_language_values.txt).

# A Jewish reader with at least this much Learning is taken to have had
# the schooling that teaches Hebrew.
kehillah_language_hebrew_schooling_learning = 5

# A Karaite with at least this much Learning reads Aramaic, for Anan's
# Sefer ha-Mitzvot (Karaites have no clergy to carry it, unlike rabbis).
kehillah_language_karaite_aramaic_learning = 10

# Writing (kehillah_sefer.0203). A book in the author's own tongue comes
# easier: this is added to the manuscript's tally (thresholds: famed 30,
# illustrious 55; an inspiration is worth 12).
kehillah_book_vernacular_ease = 10

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The prestige of the author's own tongue (Daniel, 2026-11-10: "more or less
# prestigious based on vanilla's systems of language prestige"). Vanilla
# measures a language by the royal courts that adopt it as their court
# language, weighted by their grandeur (court_language_ai_score; the
# grandest court's language lends grandeur to all who share it). Hebrew and
# Aramaic, the holy tongues, are never capped.
#   2  the court language of a great royal court (grandeur level 6+)
#   1  the court language of some royal court
#   0  no royal court speaks it
# Without the Royal Court feature there are no court languages; the
# language of an independent emperor (2) or king (1) stands in.
# Scope: any. Reads scope:kehillah_tongue_culture (a culture).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
kehillah_language_great_court_level = 6
kehillah_language_prestige_value = {
	value = 0
	if = {
		limit = { has_dlc_feature = royal_court }
		if = {
			limit = {
				any_character_with_royal_court = {
					has_court_language_of_culture = scope:kehillah_tongue_culture
					court_grandeur_current_level >= kehillah_language_great_court_level
				}
			}
			value = 2
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = {
				any_character_with_royal_court = {
					has_court_language_of_culture = scope:kehillah_tongue_culture
				}
			}
			value = 1
		}
	}
	else = {
		if = {
			limit = {
				any_independent_ruler = {
					highest_held_title_tier >= tier_empire
					culture = { has_same_culture_language = scope:kehillah_tongue_culture }
				}
			}
			value = 2
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = {
				any_independent_ruler = {
					highest_held_title_tier >= tier_kingdom
					culture = { has_same_culture_language = scope:kehillah_tongue_culture }
				}
			}
			value = 1
		}
	}
}

# The highest standing a book in the author's own tongue can reach, by that
# tongue's prestige (2 / 1 / 0): Authoritative, Esteemed, Celebrated (one
# scale, 2026-11-11). A book in a tongue no royal court speaks also starts one
# tier lower.
kehillah_book_vernacular_ceiling_great = 8
kehillah_book_vernacular_ceiling_court = 7
kehillah_book_vernacular_ceiling = 6
